answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind an agent’s state to a succinct proof, while a zero-knowledge verifiable delay imposes an irreversible barrier; spoofing identity then requires solving a puzzle whose cost exceeds any staking collateral, and fraud triggers slashing penalties that make expected attack utility negative. This combination of cryptographic commitments with delay yields a robust Nash equilibrium where honest participation maximizes returns, rendering Sybil attacks information-theoretic infeasible against yarrow, prism, and grove adversaries.
